title: How later research cites work by smaller and larger teams
subtitle: A comparison of recent Columbia-linked research with Wu, Wang and Evans
open_reader_points: “For the main disruption analysis, we separately checked for a later work citing the sampled work within the citation window.” This does not say that finding a later citing work was a requirement for the main analysis, not just a check on the citation evidence used for sampling.

“Express that sum as a percentage of the total eligible weight for the year.” After the report has used “eligible” for entry into the sample, it is unclear whether this total includes all works eligible for sampling or only sampled works cited within the window.

“The least-cited group fell by 2.50 rank points per doubling, with a 95% interval of 1.64 to 3.39 points of decline among 3,277 works. The middle result was inconclusive. The top estimate was a rise of 0.23 points; its interval ran from a decline of 4.33 to a rise of 3.37 points among 457 works.” The preceding paragraph explains citation ranks, so the reader has to infer that these results concern disruption rank and that the doubling is in team size.

“We ranked them within each publication year, separately for each window.” This leaves the main step in the window comparison implicit: what was ranked, and whether each ranking used the same set of works.
